response: Yes, bipolar disorders are often underdiagnosed in patients with depressive episodes. This is because the depressive episodes in bipolar disorder can be similar to those experienced in major depressive disorder, making it challenging to distinguish between the two conditions. As a result, many patients with bipolar disorder are initially misdiagnosed with major depressive disorder, and it may take several episodes or a manic/hypomanic episode to correctly diagnose bipolar disorder. Studies have shown that it can take an average of 5-10 years for a patient with bipolar disorder to receive an accurate diagnosis, highlighting the need for careful evaluation and monitoring of patients with depressive episodes to ensure accurate diagnosis and treatment.
